questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: What is the general formula for the distance $d$ between two points $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ in a 2-D Cartesian plane?
questions.explanationAnswer: The distance formula derived from the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem is $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$.
questions.explanationQuestion: Requires recall of the coordinate geometry distance formula.

questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: When a triangle is reflected across the y-axis, the lengths of its sides change compared to the original triangle.
questions.explanationAnswer: Reflection is an isometry, meaning it preserves distances (side lengths) between points.
questions.explanationQuestion: Requires recall of properties of geometric transformations.

questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: In the triangle ADM (Fig 1.6), to find the distance AD, we calculate the horizontal distance as the difference in ______ coordinates and the vertical distance as the difference in ______ coordinates.
questions.explanationAnswer: The horizontal shift is $\Delta x$ and the vertical shift is $\Delta y$.
questions.explanationQuestion: Requires understanding how to decompose 2D distance into components.

questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions allow for the simple calculation of distance using absolute differences $|x_2 - x_1|$ or $|y_2 - y_1|$?

options.optionText: When the line segment is parallel to the x-axis
When the line segment is parallel to the y-axis
When the points are at the origin
When the line segment is diagonal

multi: When the line segment is parallel to the x-axis
When the line segment is parallel to the y-axis
questions.explanationAnswer: Distance is calculated as the absolute difference of the varying coordinate if the other coordinate remains constant.
questions.explanationQuestion: Requires comprehension of the distance formula's simplified cases.

questions.topic: Page 9: 1.4 DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO POINTS IN THE 2-D PLANE (Pages 9-10 Focus)
questions.questionText: If a circle has its center at the origin $(0, 0)$ and passes through point $P(-3, 4)$, what is the radius of the circle?

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Understand that the radius is the distance from the center $(0,0)$ to any point on the circumference.

questions.explanationAnswer: The radius is the distance from $(0,0)$ to $(-3,4)$, which is $\sqrt{(-3)^2 + 4^2} = 5$.
questions.explanationQuestion: Application of distance formula to circle geometry.
